newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL Alberta oil line suffers rupture.
newsitem.headline: IPL Alberta oil line suffers rupture.

text.p: A rupture on an IPL Energy Inc crude oil pipeline in Alberta forced a 20-hour shutdown of the line late Friday, an IPL spokesman said on Monday.

The rupture, which occurred about 70 miles southeast of Edmonton on IPL's Line 3, was repaired about 20 hours after it was discovered and the pipeline was brought back into full service on Sunday, IPL's Alan Roth said.

Roth said about 6,500 barrels of oil spilled at the company's Strome pumping station on the 650,000 barrel per day Line 3, which moves mostly medium and heavy crudes to Superior, Wisconsin from Edmonton.
"Line 3 was put back in service about 20 hours after being shut down and they bypassed Strome while they did the repair," he said.
"The repair was completed by Sunday morning and everything went back up -- pumps started and that kind of thing."

Crude oil volumes on the system, which feeds refineries in the U.S. Midwest and southern Ontario with western Canadian supply, had already been lower than last year and no rationing of capacity had been required for March.
"The amount of throughput that we lost as a result of this operational problem on the weekend will be made up I think fairly handily by the end of March," Roth said.
No landowners in the area were directly affected by the spill and cleanup operations were underway, he said.
